mcqs.learning_point: Different forms in which matter is encountered
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the three common forms in which matter is encountered in everyday life?

options.A: Solids have a fixed shape and volume, liquids have a fixed shape but no fixed volume, gases have a fixed volume but no fixed shape.
options.B: Solids have a fixed shape and volume, liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container, gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume.
options.C: Solids have no fixed shape but a fixed volume, liquids have both fixed shape and volume, gases have a fixed shape but no fixed volume.
options.D: Solids, liquids, and gases all have fixed shapes and volumes.

mcqs.answer: Solids have a fixed shape and volume, liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container, gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume.
mcqs.explanation: Solids retain both shape and volume, liquids keep volume but adopt the shape of their container, and gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume. Option B states this correctly; the other options mix up these properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Meaning of matter at the introductory level
mcqs.question: A student picks up a textbook and holds it in her hands. According to the introductory definition of matter, what term best describes the textbook?
mcqs.explanation: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. A textbook clearly has mass and takes up space, so it is matter. Energy, force, and light are not definitions of matter.

mcqs.learning_point: Examples of matter in everyday life
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of matter?
mcqs.explanation: Matter must have mass and occupy space. Air, water, and salt all satisfy this. Heat is a form of energy, not matter, so option C is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Different forms in which matter is encountered
mcqs.question: A child observes ice, water, and steam. Which statement correctly matches each substance with the form of matter it represents?

options.A: Ice – liquid, Water – solid, Steam – gas
options.B: Ice – solid, Water – liquid, Steam – gas
options.C: Ice – gas, Water – solid, Steam – liquid
options.D: Ice – solid, Water – gas, Steam – liquid

mcqs.answer: Ice – solid, Water – liquid, Steam – gas
mcqs.explanation: Ice is a solid, water is a liquid, and steam (water vapor) is a gas. Option B reflects this correctly; the other options assign incorrect states.

mcqs.learning_point: Meaning of matter at the introductory level
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about matter?

options.C: Matter can be created or destroyed easily
options.D: Matter can be felt when touched

mcqs.answer: Matter can be created or destroyed easily
mcqs.explanation: While matter does occupy space and has mass, the law of conservation of matter states it cannot be created or destroyed in ordinary chemical processes. Option C is a misconception; the others are true statements about matter.

mcqs.learning_point: Examples of matter in everyday life
mcqs.question: Why is a wooden chair considered matter?

options.A: Because it can change its temperature
options.B: Because it occupies space and has mass
options.D: Because it can move on its own

mcqs.answer: Because it occupies space and has mass
mcqs.explanation: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and occupies space. A wooden chair clearly does both, making option B correct. Temperature change, light production, and self‑movement are not criteria for being matter.

mcqs.learning_point: Different forms in which matter is encountered
mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons of solids, liquids, and gases is entirely correct?

options.A: Solids have a definite shape, liquids have a definite shape, gases have a definite shape
options.B: Solids have a definite volume, liquids have a definite volume, gases have a definite volume
options.C: Solids have tightly packed particles that vibrate in place, liquids have particles that are close but can slide past each other, gases have particles far apart that move freely
options.D: All three have particles arranged in a regular lattice

mcqs.answer: Solids have tightly packed particles that vibrate in place, liquids have particles that are close but can slide past each other, gases have particles far apart that move freely
mcqs.explanation: Option C accurately describes particle arrangement and movement in the three states. Options A and B incorrectly assign shape or volume to all three, and D is false because only solids (and some liquids) have regular lattices.

mcqs.learning_point: Meaning of matter at the introductory level
mcqs.question: According to the NCERT definition for Class 6, matter is best defined as:

options.A: Anything that can be seen with the naked eye
options.B: Anything that has mass and occupies space
options.D: Anything that can move on its own

mcqs.answer: Anything that has mass and occupies space
mcqs.explanation: The NCERT textbook defines matter as anything that has mass and occupies space. Visibility, heat production, or autonomous movement are not part of the definition, making option B the correct choice.
